stories.headline: How Scott Colom won his longshot bid to flip Mississippi's Senate seat
stories.summary: In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom won his longshot bid to oust incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. Colom's victory is a stunning reversal in the deeply conservative state that hasn't been represented by a Black senator since the Reconstruction era following the Civil War.

sources.title: PBS NewsHour: How Scott Colom won his longshot bid to flip Mississippi's Senate seat
NPR: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from DA to Mississippi's Democratic…

stories.now: NPR: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics.
stories.backstory: Republicans have held both chambers since January 2025, and all 435 House seats and about a third of the Senate were on the ballot. More than 53 million Americans voted early. Tariffs and high gas prices tied to the Iran war weighed on Trump's approval, and recent polls gave Democrats an edge in most key Senate races. Courts also turned back a Trump administration bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots.
